subsystems.name: State-capture array
subsystems.role: would measure the position, type and state of essentially every atom and molecule in the body.

subsystems.name: Information record
subsystems.role: the snapshot itself — an encoded description of the organism at one instant.

subsystems.name: Computational model
subsystems.role: software that knows which molecular states are 'the same person' and which are damage to be corrected.

subsystems.name: Reconstruction apparatus
subsystems.role: would rebuild or restore the molecular structure described by the record.

subsystems.name: Verification system
subsystems.role: confirms that the restored organism matches the captured state and is functional.

buildSteps.title: Arrest all motion
buildSteps.detail: At body temperature molecules move and react billions of times a second, so the first step would be to stop metabolism and diffusion without destroying structure — for example by deep cooling.

buildSteps.title: Scan at atomic resolution
buildSteps.detail: Read out the position and state of every atom. This is where known physics bites: measurement cannot capture position and momentum together to arbitrary precision, and unknown quantum states cannot be copied exactly.

buildSteps.title: Encode the record
buildSteps.detail: Turn the readings into a stable, error-corrected data set. Even a rough estimate puts the information content of a human body far beyond any storage that exists, by many orders of magnitude.

buildSteps.title: Store it
buildSteps.detail: Keep the record intact and readable for as long as needed — years, decades or longer.

buildSteps.title: Decide what to restore
buildSteps.detail: Compare the captured state against a 'healthy' model and mark the accumulated damage — plaques, mutations, cross-links, lost cells — for reversal.

buildSteps.title: Rebuild the structure
buildSteps.detail: In principle, rebuild the molecular arrangement the record describes, either by assembling molecules directly or by editing an existing body back toward that state.

buildSteps.title: Restore function
buildSteps.detail: Restart metabolism and confirm the organism is alive, intact and identical in the ways that matter.

prerequisites.tech: Non-destructive atomic-resolution imaging of a whole organism
prerequisites.why: today's atomic-resolution methods work on small, fixed samples, not living bodies, and destroy or fix most tissue.
the uncertainty principle and the no-cloning theorem make a perfect, lossless copy of an unknown quantum state impossible in principle.
chemists can synthesise individual molecules, but nothing approaches rebuilding a whole cell atom by atom.

prerequisites.tech: Exascale computational model of a whole organism
prerequisites.why: the model must identify which molecular differences are damage and which are the person, and simulate them all at once.

prerequisites.tech: Storage at something like the body's full information content
prerequisites.why: the data volume is astronomically larger than current global storage.

pathway.milestone: high-resolution connectomics and cryo-preservation studies of small tissue samples
pathway.unlocks: evidence that structure can be mapped and partly preserved after death.

pathway.milestone: routine, error-corrected mapping and synthesis of individual cells
pathway.unlocks: proof that a cell's molecular state can be recorded and compared.

pathway.milestone: reversible stasis — safely arresting and restarting metabolism in whole organs
pathway.unlocks: a way to hold a body still long enough to work on it.

pathway.milestone: theoretical test of whether complete capture and rebuild is physically possible at all
pathway.unlocks: either a genuine route to damage-free restoration, or proof that the concept is impossible and effort belongs in ordinary medicine.
